probes.note: baseline: both parsers accept, both report the parse end at the last byte
THE distinguishing case. require_null_terminated needs a NUL INSIDE the buffer: the length form has none and fails, the string form re-derives strlen+1 and therefore always has one
same bytes plus one NUL: now the length form accepts too
the option skips whitespace FIRST, and the reported end is after the skip (probed: 10, not 7) -- the back-up quirk in buffer_skip_whitespace is what lands the offset on the terminator
trailing garbage: rejected by both parsers, error position at the garbage
the same bytes without the option: accepted, end at 7 -- the laxness that require_null_terminated exists to turn off
an embedded NUL splits the two entry points: the length form sees past it and rejects the garbage, the string form's strlen stops at it and accepts

cJSON's parse_string rewinds to a pointer initialized BEFORE it validates anything, so a non-quote object key reports the offset PAST it (2, not 1). This probe is the regression for a real port divergence
same class, reached by a comma where a key belongs
same class after a complete member: the C reports 8 for 8 bytes
parse_array's failure does NOT rewind -- the offset is where parse_value gave up (3), which is why the key case above is worth its own probe
runs off the end: the position clamps to the last valid index
no value at all: position 0
whitespace only -- the skip walks onto the terminator and backs up, so the position is the last index, not 0
an empty document: the length form takes cJSON's `0 == buffer_length` refusal, the string form gets a 1-byte buffer holding only the NUL and fails in the parser instead
prebuffer < 0 is cJSON_PrintBuffered's ONLY guard (cJSON.c:1278) and the only behavior the prebuffer size has

prebuffer 0 still grows: the buffer is not noalloc, so the bytes match an unbuffered print. (The C's answer here depends on malloc(0) being non-NULL; the port's does not -- DIVERGENCES.md, structural eliminations)
a prebuffer far smaller than the output: every ensure reallocs and the result is unchanged
strlen + 2, the smallest buffer that fits: the extra byte over strlen+1 is ensure's reserved NUL slot
a zero-length buffer: refused before anything is written
length < 0 is refused by the MODE on both sides -- the port's &mut [u8] cannot spell a negative length, so the guard has no core to live in
a fuzz-sized request, clamped to CJSON_OPTS_MAX_BUF by both sides
format=1 exercises the separator, indent and close sites with their formatted lengths
nesting deep enough that print_object's close asks for depth+1, not 2
the formatted boundary is strlen+2 of the FORMATTED bytes, which is a different number from the unformatted one
both bits set at once
a bare literal: ensure(5) at offset 0, so 6 bytes is the boundary
the widest literal: ensure(6)
escapes make print_string's output_length exceed the input length, which is what its ensure is computed from
a <32 byte costs 5 extra output bytes (\u00xx), the other escape width
empty array and object: the loops never run, so the open and close sites are adjacent
nothing parses: the printers still run their guards and report `-`
